div.div: Data Intelligence and Governance for Splunk: understand what your data can support, where it is thin, and what to improve next.

div.p: DIG Navigator is an evidence app for Splunk data readiness. It helps you see how usable your telemetry is for operations, detection, investigation, and governance conversations.
DIG samples a scope you choose and shows potential evidence for:

ul.li: Structure and quality of the events you are collecting
CIM / datamodel readiness based on observed fields and tags
Governance alignment as recommended-field completeness against mapped frameworks (potential evidence, not a compliance score)
Delivery and timeliness of telemetry arriving into Splunk

div.p: DIG does not replace Splunk expertise, formal audits, or control testing. It gives admins, engineers, analysts, and governance stakeholders a shared place to decide what to improve next.

ol.li: Open Configuration and create or refresh the lookups that power DIG (CIM field catalog, governance mapping, and related seed data).
Set an Analysis Scope (search, time range, group-by, sample limit) and click Apply Scope so DIG remembers it for you.
Data Intelligence (executive view): structure, quality, CIM alignment, and datamodel readiness for the scoped data.
Data Governance (executive view): framework / control potential-evidence completeness and source footprint.
DIG IN (investigation views): drill from an executive panel, or open an IN dashboard directly, to explain why a finding looks the way it does.
Act on the evidence: improve extractions, CIM tags, onboarding, governance mappings, or timeliness rules as needed.

ul.li: Structure IN: data shape and classification detail
Readiness IN: datamodel / CIM readiness investigation
Governance IN: control, capability, and mapping explainability
Quality IN: quality dimensions in more depth
Delivery IN: ingest delay and timestamp integrity

div.p: Executive dashboards answer “what should I look at?” IN dashboards answer “why, and what evidence supports that?”

If DIG surfaces issues but the remediation path is unclear, Dev/Null Security can help turn the evidence into a practical plan for Splunk onboarding, CIM alignment, governance design, telemetry readiness, and Enterprise Security enablement.
Found a bug, want a feature, or have feedback on DIG? Open an issue on the public GitHub repository so we can track and respond.
